review.verbatim_critique:
[D0.5.G cold referee] delivered tier=subfield below novelty_target=field (floor=field). The note delivers exactly one thing: a one-sided lower bound R_n^NP >= c(log n/n)^{1/4} for the CTY law class, improving the published n^{-1/4} converse by a single logarithmic factor. There is no upper bound anywhere in the note; the only achievability invoked is the comparator's own theorem, which the note concedes holds only on its Assumption 2 subclass and which it never checks against its own square-support witness — so no matched rate, no frontier, and no resolution of the two-sided conjecture is delivered, only its lower half. The minimax is taken over a restricted decision class T_n^NP in which a single law-independent map T_n sees x only through the distance-compressed sample; the claim that this is 'the inherited CTY estimator architecture, not an extra restriction' is asserted in the Interpretation section and never established by quoting the comparator's class, so the load-bearing comparability of the strengthened converse rests on assertion. The note is also a heavy shrink of its own stated topic: the advertised exact rate, the straight-design L>4 versus L=4 distance/full-location elbow characterization, the smooth-geometry saturation, and the order-m joint-coarea upper rates with matching converses are entirely absent from the statements. Internally the framing is honest — the Honest Scope and limitation sections correctly disclaim any matched frontier — and the two lemmas (angular-perturbation packing that equalizes the radial marginal, and the hypercube/overlap decentralized-decoding certificate) plus the Poissonization–de-Poissonization argument appear correct; the shortfall is scope, not error.

DIRECTED IMPROVEMENT (re-derive the SAME object implementing this, do not reproduce the prior note): Deliver the achievability half on the same estimand: either prove that the packing laws lie in the Assumption 2 subclass so the comparator's uniform upper theorem matches the new converse at (log n/n)^{1/4}, or construct a distance-based estimator (local-polynomial-in-distance with a boundary-adaptive bandwidth) attaining the uniform rate under rectifiability alone, and additionally pin the decision class by quoting CTY Theorem 6's estimator class verbatim so the 'inherited, not extra' restriction is proved rather than asserted.

proposed_assumption.label: A-usm-boundary-sup
proposed_assumption.statement: (Universally measurable boundary supremum.) For every n \geq 2, every P \in \mathcal P_{\mathrm{NP}}(L,q) and every \widehat\mu_n \in \mathcal T_n^{\mathrm{NP}}, the map \mathbf z = ((y_i,\xi_i)_{i\leq n}) \mapsto \sup_{x\in\operatorname{bd}(\mathcal X_P)} |\widehat\mu_n(\mathbf z)(x)-\mu_P(x)| \in [0,\infty] admits a version measurable with respect to the P^{\otimes n}-completion of the product \sigma-algebra on the sample space, and the completed expectation \mathbb E_P of that version equals the outer expectation \mathbb E_P^{*} of the map itself. All occurrences of \mathbb E_P in def:cty-distance-risk are understood as this completed expectation.
proposed_assumption.source: This is exactly the conclusion the .tex derives at writeup.tex:475 from universal measurability of analytic (upper semianalytic) sets under every completed probability measure — Choquet capacitability, a standard classical measure-theoretic fact with no Mathlib formalization. It is a regularity bridge about the measurability of the loss functional, not about the class \mathcal P_{\mathrm{NP}}(L,q) or the log-penalty rate the conjecture characterizes, so it is generic and costs no headline novelty.
